temperature.title: Regenerative heating with flash vapour
temperature.description: Vapour flashed from the hot digested slurry (multi-stage flash) is condensed in these heaters to preheat the incoming slurry — recovering most of the heat. Desilication product scale (sodalite) and titanate deposits build up inside the tubes and cut heat transfer, so heaters are taken off-line for descaling (hydro-blasting or acid) in rotation.

video_tutorials.title: Digestion Heater — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Digestion Heater.
Digestion heaters are shell & tube exchangers that preheat the bauxite slurry before digestion.
Slurry passes several times through the tubes while flash vapour from the multi-stage flash tanks condenses on the outside.
Typical applications include regenerative slurry heating before digestion; heating with flash vapour from blow-off tanks; final heating with live steam (last heaters).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Shell (vapour side) & Tubesheets, Top & Bottom Channel Heads with Pass Partitions (slurry makes several passes).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Digestion Heater — Operation

script.narration: How the Digestion Heater works.
Slurry enters the bottom channel head.
It makes several passes through the tubes.
Flash vapour condenses in the shell.
Condensate and non-condensables are removed.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Vapour flashed from the hot digested slurry (multi-stage flash) is condensed in these heaters to preheat the incoming slurry — recovering most of the heat.

video_tutorials.title: Digestion Heater — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Digestion Heater.
Monitor approach temperatures.
Descaling (hydro-blasting/acid).
Tube replacement.
Watch for scaling: lower outlet temperature. Common cause: dsp, titanate.
Watch for tube leaks: slurry in condensate. Common cause: erosion.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
